The '''Imperial Script Reform of 1725''' was an early imperial reform of the [[Vesperan Alphabet]]. Source material describes it as the point at which the [[Imperial Language Academy]] refined the script for imperial printing, administration, diplomacy, and public inscriptions.

== Background ==

The reform followed the [[Imperial Proclamation of 1710]] and the establishment of the Imperial Language Academy in 1715. The early empire needed written standards that could support mass records, provincial administration, treaty correspondence, military orders, and monumental ceremony.

== Effects ==

The reform standardized printed type, simplified administrative handwriting, created diplomatic forms for foreign correspondence, and regularized monumental inscription styles used in state architecture and religious settings.

The reform also strengthened the relationship between script and imperial authority. Written Vesperan became easier to reproduce, teach, and inspect across a growing bureaucracy.

== Legacy ==

Later scholars treated the reform as one of the major reasons Imperial Vesperan records remained relatively consistent across the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries. The reform also influenced post-imperial preservation of archives after the empire's collapse in 1949.
